message.content: {"4": {"original": "discrimination against music lovers", "rephrased": "The blanket ban on the legal music service Spotify by the University of Oxford constitutes discrimination against music lovers, unfairly penalizing a specific group of students who wish to access lawful content.", "summary": "Students characterize the university's blanket ban on the legal music service Spotify as discriminatory."}, "5": {"original": "see nothing wrong with students using Spotify", "rephrased": "Many students at the University of Oxford see nothing wrong with their peers using the legal streaming service Spotify, viewing the prohibition as an unnecessary restriction on lawful access to music.", "summary": "Students argue that prohibiting access to the legal music service Spotify is an unjustified restriction."}, "6": {"original": "Reports indicate the ban had inconsistencies, allowing some students to connect,", "rephrased": "Reports indicate that the University of Oxford's ban on the peer-to-peer music service Spotify has been applied inconsistently, with some students still able to connect to the service despite the official restrictions.", "summary": "The university's ban on the peer-to-peer music service Spotify has been applied inconsistently across the campus."}, "7": {"original": "Bandwidth usage scales up significantly with thousands of users, making the ban", "rephrased": "The Computer Services department at the University of Oxford argues that the ban on the peer-to-peer music service Spotify is necessary because bandwidth usage scales significantly with thousands of users, threatening the network capacity required for academic work.", "summary": "The university argues that banning the peer-to-peer music service Spotify is necessary to preserve network bandwidth for academic purposes."}}
